subject: Regional acceptance checklist & VPC handover — Meditech PoC
messages:
From: Sara Holt <sara.holt@meditech.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Regional acceptance checklist & VPC handover — Meditech PoC

Hi Laura / Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Meditech is ready to move the PoC toward an EU-only acceptance run. Before we kick off our security review & procurement steps, can you confirm the following at a level we can present to our InfoSec/Procurement teams? We need items we can land on within the week: 

1) Can you confirm the PoC will be hosted in your EU region only (no multi-region failover during the PoC)?
2) Outline the VPC/private connectivity options for PoC: private peering, transit, and whether a PrivateLink is available.
3) KMS model: do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for the PoC, and are keys protected by an HSM?
4) Quick inventory of SOC 2 / CAIQ / SIG materials you can share (redacted artifacts are fine).
5) Any operator/engineer access during the PoC and what controls/monitoring you have in place (auditing, jump-box, bastion, time-limited access).

Our timeline: security review by Tue 10/6, procurement contract draft by 10/8, and technical handover immediately after acceptance. Can you provide a single packet we can hand to our InfoSec (or a link with the items above)?

If easier, happy to do a 20-minute tech sync Monday — Sara and our security lead will join.

Thanks,
Sara Holt
Senior Security Program Manager
Meditech Health
[sara.holt@meditech.com]

[Attachment: initial_meditech_requirements.docx (doc)]

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely put together a handoff packet. Quick clarifications so we prepare exactly what you need: 

- For the PoC window, are you asking that we disable cross-region failover entirely, or simply confirm no automatic failover will be enabled unless you explicitly request it?
- For KMS: do you require an HSM-backed key (e.g., Cloud HSM) for the PoC, or would an AWS KMS CMK with BYOK suffice as a first step?

We’ll prepare: a short SOC 2 summary (redacted), a CAIQ slice answering your top 25 questions, an EU-hosting matrix that maps controls to evidence, and a VPC peering runbook. Monica will draft the technical runbook and the matrix; Jonas will confirm network egress paths and ops on-call.

If Monday works, how about 10:00 AM CET / 1:00 AM PDT? (We can shift earlier/later if needed.)

Best,

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holt <sara.holt@meditech.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Regional acceptance checklist & VPC handover — Meditech PoC

Hi Sara — taking the ops/controls side here and attaching the packet for your review. Summary below; full artifacts in attachments.

TL;DR: PoC can be EU-only, private peering supported, BYOK with HSM-backed option available, limited operator access.

What we attached:
- eu-hosting-matrix.xlsx — map of hosting controls to artifacts and environment IDs (contains region tags, node inventory, and tenant mapping).
- meditech_caIQ_slice.pdf — CAIQ answers focused on residency, networking, key management, and logging (we highlighted answers most relevant to Meditech).
- vpc-peering-runbook.txt — step-by-step for setting up dedicated VPC peering + validation checks.
- soc2-summary-2026.pdf — one-page SOC 2 summary (redacted scope & auditor).

Key points (excerpt):
- Region: We will schedule your PoC in eu-west-1 (AWS) nodes; no automatic cross-region replication will be enabled for the PoC unless you request failover testing. The eu environment uses isolated subnets per-tenant and customer-dedicated compute groups for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Private connectivity: We support AWS PrivateLink and VPC peering. For PoC we recommend direct VPC peering with route tables restricted to the Meditech CIDR; private IPs only. Transit options are documented in the runbook.
- KMS / Key custody: Two options available for the PoC: (A) Redwood-managed CMK (AWS KMS) with restricted operator access and audit logging; (B) Customer-managed keys (BYOK) where Meditech uploads keys to your own AWS KMS or CloudHSM — we support CloudHSM-backed keys for HSM protection. For onboarding speed we suggest (B) if you want HSM-backed keys from day one; otherwise we can start on (A) and rotate to BYOK once procurement finishes. We have documented key-handling procedures in the runbook (key import steps, key rotation windows, and emergency-revocation flow).
- Operator access and auditing: Operator access is time-bound, invoked through our bastion workflow with TOTP + limited SSH jump accounts; all sessions are recorded. We provide audit logs for session start/stop and API-level access (trace IDs included).
- Egress and logging: No public egress by default; outbound NAT only via controlled egress nodes with retained flow logs and per-tenant logging retention policy (we included retention windows in the matrix).

Next steps we recommend:
1) Confirm desired KMS option (BYOK w/ HSM or Redwood-managed) so we can include the key-import steps in the PoC runbook.
2) Review attachments and flag any questions — we can produce an expanded CAIQ or full SIG-lite on request.
3) Confirm a tech sync slot and we’ll bring the engineer who owns peering.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

[Attachments: eu-hosting-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), meditech_caIQ_slice.pdf (pdf), vpc-peering-runbook.txt (text), soc2-summary-2026.pdf (pdf)]

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Sara
